races.name: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Airds Moss
runners_data.note: Front-runner trained by David Harry Kelly, won over this exact trip on Good ground last time (form 4/32-1), and Mark Walsh in the saddle adds significant tactical intelligence; best profile to seize and hold the lead cleanly.

runners_data.name: Individualism
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a 5yo bumper/hurdle background under a 5lb claimer; sim-going record shows 14 runs on Good with very modest returns, and the style and jockey combination makes this a bigger ask than the odds might suggest.

runners_data.name: Minella Hollow
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed four times in five starts over 2m hurdles on Good, winning once; freshened up after 18 days, trips and going are squarely in his comfort zone, and Daniel King's waiting tactics suit a strong-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Reaching High
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins and Willie Mullins combine, and the 2/12f Good run shows raw ability, though only two wins from 11 qualifying starts on this going and the unknown hurdles form (/-) mean significant uncertainty despite the pedigree of the stable.

runners_data.name: Kingstonian
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Joseph Patrick O'Brien with JJ Slevin aboard — won over 12f on Good, placed at 18f, but the hot pace battle means he may be outgunned for the lead by Airds Moss; if he leads he's dangerous, if he scraps for it he may be found out.

runners_data.name: Kilbeg Jimmy
runners_data.note: Completely unknown quantity — no last-run date, no form string, listed UNKNOWN going concern and lightly raced flag; style is undefined (U) so impossible to map meaningfully into this shape.

runners_data.name: Market Square
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner for Emmet Mullins but both runs show modest finishes (9th and 5th) and headgear (hg:h) indicates a horse that needs restraining encouragement; in a five-way pace battle, getting to the front cleanly looks difficult.

runners_data.name: Papanell
runners_data.note: Undefined style with 198 days off the track — the long layoff is the key flag here; placed once from three Good-ground starts, but the inactivity and unknown headgear situation make this speculative in a competitive 19-runner field.

runners_data.name: Penny Express
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Gordon Elliott with Jack Kennedy in the saddle — has placed four times from 12 Good-ground starts but never won; the pace he helps create is unlikely to benefit him when he's one of five making the running.

runners_data.name: Rockstar Rebel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a single run to his name — 11th on Good — tagged as fading in finish, and with an amateur jockey (7lb claimer) this looks a learning exercise rather than a winning proposition in a field this size.

runners_data.name: Well Bud
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Eoin McCarthy, placed once from two Good-ground hurdle starts; the tongue-tie (hg:t) suggests breathing was a concern, and in a five-way battle for the lead he risks burning too much petrol too soon.

runners_data.name: Local Resident
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4yo with going listed UNKNOWN and only one placing from two career starts; 174 days off the track compounds the uncertainty and Reserve jockey Danny Gilligan has minimal information to go on tactically.

runners_data.name: Sea Limit
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with a single 9th from one Good-ground start and a fade-in-finish flag; 12 days since last run is fine, but there is simply insufficient evidence to trust this horse's stamina over 2m½f against more experienced rivals.

runners_data.name: The Orphan Girl
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with back-to-back 9ths on Good ground and a clear fade-in-finish tag; form string 341-99 shows earlier ability elsewhere but the recent Killarney-distance form is discouraging under an amateur 7lb claimer.

runners_data.name: Windy Grey
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a fade flag and an 8th, a pulled-up, and a 14th in recent starts; the SOF and HEA going history is at odds with today's Good, and three poor runs in a row makes this hard to recommend in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Misty Valentine
runners_data.note: 4yo hold-up type with just a 15th and a pulled-up to show — both on Good — and a fade-in-finish tag; a 7lb claimer in the saddle and 19 days between runs does not overcome the lack of any encouraging evidence.

runners_data.name: Eben Zaabeel
runners_data.note: Lightly raced AJ Martin runner who is a genuine hold-up horse in nature but has been placed in midfield on the map because of field congestion at the rear; the tongue-tie flags a breathing angle, and five runs without a win on Good ground (best effort a 3rd on Soft) means the style displacement further dims an already modest profile.

runners_data.name: Colliers Quay
runners_data.note: Undefined style runner with Reserve jockey and a single 5th from one Good-ground start; the lightly raced flag and reserve booking mean connections may not have a clear tactical plan, making this difficult to factor into any scenario.

runners_data.name: Man Down
runners_data.note: Going listed UNKNOWN, lightly raced flag, and a Reserve jockey booking — four career starts show two pulls-up and a 4th, with 97 days between runs; this is a horse gaining experience rather than contesting for the win.

races.paceDynamic: Airds Moss, Kingstonian, Market Square, Well Bud, and Penny Express are all confirmed front-runners in a 19-runner maiden hurdle over 2m½f on Good ground at Killarney, guaranteeing a strong, sustained gallop from the outset with multiple horses fighting for position and the rail in the opening furlongs. That volume of pace will compress the early running into a scrappy, high-tempo affair where no single lead horse dictates comfortably — the fractions will be honest to fast throughout, burning off one-dimensional speedsters and testing stamina sharply in the closing stages. Eben Zaabeel is a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Airds Moss and Kingstonian are most likely to actually lead given their recent positional form. The race shape strongly favours horses racing from a prominent-to-midfield position with proven stamina and a clean jumping record — they can sit just off the pace battle without burning energy early, then pick up the pieces as the front-runners tie each other up from the home turn.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stayer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners force a genuine end-to-end gallop that cracks the pace-setters turning in, a well-positioned stayer rolling through from mid-division claims it.
scenarios.body: The leaders burn each other out through honest fractions on Good ground, and by the second-last hurdle the pace-setters are spent, leaving the race to a resolute traveller who has been coasting in the first half of midfield. Horses with proven stamina at this trip, clean jumping, and a prominent-but-not-leading berth are ideally profiled.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner — most likely Airds Moss or Kingstonian — seizes a clear lead and the pace paradoxically steadies as rivals cancel each other out.
scenarios.body: With so many speed horses in the race, jockeys may check rather than chase, accidentally gifting a clean lead to whoever gets to the front most fluently; on Good Killarney ground a horse controlling from the front with jumping accuracy could steal enough margin to hold on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early gallop strings the field out and a prominent-to-midfield horse with superior class picks off the tiring leaders from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Minella Hollow, who has placed consistently at this trip on Good ground, or Reaching High under Danny Mullins from the powerful Mullins yard could track the pace without expense and deliver a smooth run to the line. Their jumping quality becomes decisive when the leaders' errors accumulate under fatigue.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly extreme and the leaders implode spectacularly in the final half-mile, creating a gap for a late-running horse to swoop.
scenarios.body: This shape is the least likely given that most genuine hold-up types are either lightly raced unknowns or have been redistributed forward due to field congestion; Individualism has the form profile but a modest record in similar going. The probability is real but firmly discounted because the true closers in this field lack the class or recent evidence to exploit it reliably.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a fierce battle between Airds Moss, Kingstonian, Market Square, and Well Bud in the first half-mile — whichever of these emerges in front cleanly by the first hurdle without burning energy in the scrap will be the most dangerous pace horse in the race.

Penny Express (Jack Kennedy) is a respected booking for Gordon Elliott but is one of five confirmed front-runners — if Kennedy is forced to wrestle for position rather than dictate, the energy cost could compromise his finish entirely.

Reaching High has posted a suspicious 20th on Good ground last time out despite winning at 14f on Standard; watch the market move closely as the Mullins yard rarely runs horses this far below their level without an upgrade in view.

Minella Hollow's consistency (four placings in five runs) is quietly notable in a field full of lightly raced or inconsistent sorts — watch how Daniel King positions him in the first half; if he settles just off the pace battle he becomes a serious player late.

Reserve jockey bookings for Eben Zaabeel, Colliers Quay, and Man Down are worth monitoring at declaration — a named jockey upgrade, particularly for Eben Zaabeel from the AJ Martin yard, would be a meaningful market signal worth tracking before post time.

races.name: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Approval
runners_data.note: Wears hood and has run over this trip on Good before (5th, 16f, Good), but has a trainer striking at 0/9 over 14 days and 84 days off; a natural hold-up horse who in an 18-runner field will struggle to find clear daylight off a slow pace.

runners_data.name: Ealu Tapa
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on Good last time (1st, 16f, Good) and trainer Fahey is in decent form, but this horse's instinct to settle deep means it is carrying a positional penalty in a race where the pace is unlikely to create a gap to exploit late.

runners_data.name: Molto Amichi
runners_data.note: Has won over 8f on Good and placed over 9f, making this 2m½f trip a significant stamina question, though the form string (F-) suggests hurdling was interrupted; Michael Kenneally (5lb claim) could help settle the horse, but distance is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Sea Eagle
runners_data.note: Ran 2nd over 17f on Good on comeback 15 days ago and has had a recent prep, but trainer Gerard O'Leary has only one strike from six in the past fortnight; instinctively a hold-up type shuffled into midfield on the map, making its positional task harder than the chart implies.

runners_data.name: Golden Handshake
runners_data.note: Flat form includes two wins over 12f on Good ground and strong course-and-distance profile, but the sole hurdles run ended in an unseated; a finisher by nature displaced into the midfield pack, needing the race to fall perfectly to show its flat-track class.

runners_data.name: Champagne Diamond
runners_data.note: Has run twice over this trip on Good (8th and 10th) and wears tongue-tie; the form string shows a consistent fader in the finish, and the style tagged Unknown with a fades-in-finish flag makes this hard to place in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Deeter
runners_data.note: 163-day absence and a solitary hurdles run on Heavy are the dominant flags; the style is Unknown and the sole form line is a pulled-up, so no reliable pace or distance profile can be drawn — pure speculation at this point.

runners_data.name: Ikalimix
runners_data.note: Oldest horse in the field at eight and has run 16th over this trip on Good last time; the redistribution puts it in midfield but its natural rear-of-field style and declining form figures (65/0-F) suggest minimal claims regardless of scenario.

runners_data.name: Le Vent d'Ex
runners_data.note: Ran a non-staying 12th over 18f on Good and then pulled up; flagged as a fader in the finish and a hold-up type, meaning the modest pace here actively works against it, and the 7lb claimer Burke Ott adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Lincoln Mill
runners_data.note: Has finished 16th and 8th in its two Good-ground hurdles and is flagged as fading in the finish; trainer Archdeacon is 0/2 in the past fortnight and this profile — hold-up, fades, moderate form — offers nothing to recommend it in the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Macoo
runners_data.note: Going preference is Unknown and there is no last-run date or form string, making this an unquantifiable runner; the 8-year-old age combined with complete form absence means it cannot be meaningfully placed in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Minella Moon Shine
runners_data.note: The one confirmed prominent runner aside from Through The Storm, and second over 16f on Good last time (2/16f/Good) is directly relevant; Daniel King takes the ride and this horse's natural position right behind the leader is the exact sweet spot in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Je Suis Celebre
runners_data.note: All hurdles runs have been over 7-10f on Good or Standard, making the step up to 2m½f a huge unknown; the flat-track form (2nd over 7f twice at the Curragh) is encouraging for ability, but stamina is the critical question on debut over this trip.

runners_data.name: Certosa
runners_data.note: Has place form over 16-20f on Good and Good-to-Soft including a 4th over 16f on Yielding, and returns just 12 days after last run; carries a 3lb claim with Williamson but is a natural hold-up horse nudged into midfield, needing a more searching pace than Through The Storm is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Kauto Empress
runners_data.note: Two runs, both resulting in 10th on Good ground over 16-17f, and flagged as fading in the finish; M Winters has no recent runners and no market angle has emerged — this profile is one of the weakest in the field under the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Marilyns Poet
runners_data.note: A single run resulting in 12th over 19f on Good, flagged as fading in the finish, 14 days ago; Eoin Walsh takes the ride but there is nothing in the form or style profile to suggest competitiveness over this trip.

runners_data.name: Cast A Cold Eye
runners_data.note: Trained by Willie Mullins (9 winners from 29 in past 14 days) which is the headline angle, and has run 5th and 6th over comparable trips on Good and Soft; the horse's instinct is to race deep and it finds itself squeezed into midfield by weight of numbers — the Mullins stable strike rate is the only meaningful hook.

runners_data.name: Through The Storm
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the architect of the pace dynamic; three runs all over 16f on varying going, finishing 4th, 6th, and 8th, so winning form is absent, but the ability to set an uncontested lead over this trip on Good ground is a tangible tactical asset that the runner list cannot replicate.

races.paceDynamic: Through The Storm is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner maiden hurdle and, with no meaningful pressure likely to materialize early, should bowl along at a sustainable, controlled gallop from the outset — setting a rhythm that suits a horse with stamina rather than raw speed. Minella Moon Shine is the only other runner with genuine prominent intentions and may track Through The Storm closely, but neither is likely to force a truly searching tempo, leaving the race to develop as a steadily-run affair that compresses late. With pace modest and the distance a testing 2m½f on Good ground, the race shape strongly favours horses with tactical versatility and a clean turn of foot in the closing stages — a genuine prominent or chase-prominent profile that can sit just off the leader without burning energy is the sweet spot here. This field carries far more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Golden Handshake, Ealu Tapa, Certosa, Cast A Cold Eye, Approval, and Sea Eagle are all natural hold-up horses displaced into midfield slots on the map, and in reality most will not find the position or the pace injection they need — Through The Storm and Minella Moon Shine are best placed to dictate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Clean Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If Through The Storm bowls along unchallenged and the modest pace means closers never generate enough momentum to close.
scenarios.body: Through The Storm dictates on its own terms at a sustainable gallop, and Minella Moon Shine tracks throughout in second, both outrunning the hold-up pack who need a faster pace to be involved; a race run this way rewards position over finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Minella Moon Shine or a redistributed horse secures an uncontested pitch close to the leader and outstays the field from the front.
scenarios.body: The pace remains honest but not punishing, and the horse who locks onto Through The Storm's girth from the second hurdle is already in the ideal position when it matters; hold-up horses that need to weave through 18 runners on Good ground are left with too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Through The Storm goes too slow early and the field bunches tightly, allowing a horse with a sharp change of gear to sprint clear from mid-division.
scenarios.body: A dawdle followed by a sprint suits the most athletic jumper in the field who can quicken two out rather than grind; Molto Amichi, with a win over this trip on Good going, could produce a late charge if the race turns into a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Grinds Field Down
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a stronger-than-expected pace fragment the field, leaving only the most resolute stayers standing.
scenarios.body: With 18 runners and several lightly raced novices, errors or interference in a compressed field could promote the most experienced jumpers to the fore; Certosa and Sea Eagle, both with hurdling miles on the clock, would benefit from rivals falling away.

watchPoints.text: Through The Storm's jumping — if it makes a significant error at an early hurdle in this 18-runner field, the already-thin pace collapses entirely and the race shape shifts away from Scenario A immediately.

Golden Handshake's ability to navigate early traffic: coming from the outside with an unseated-rider flag on its sole hurdles run, interference in the opening half-mile could end its race before it starts.

Minella Moon Shine at the first hurdle — as the only horse likely to share the front rank with Through The Storm, a jumping blunder here removes the second-string pace anchor and hands Through The Storm complete, unchallenged control.

Watch the market moves on Cast A Cold Eye (Mullins, T14: 9/29) in the 30-minute show; if this horse is sent off well-backed it signals stable confidence that could override the redistribution concern.

With 18 runners on Good turf over 2m½f, monitor the draw and early stride patterns at the tape — any horse from a wide berth that is forced wide at the first bend will concede lengths it cannot easily recover in a race likely to be run at a conservative tempo.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Deise Crystal
runners_data.note: Hold-up type in good recent form (three placed efforts from five runs on Good ground), suited by this trip but reliant on a strong pace to make ground from off the pace; five-year-old still developing, Anna McGuinness's 4lb claim a minor compensation.
runners_data.comment: Deise Crystal arrives here just 15 days after a fifth, with a third and a runner-up finish earlier in his last five starts, though a pulled-up run in that spell tempers the picture, and he has run over today's trip and going before carrying 166 lb; the chief concern is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Pure Logic
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner who will enjoy an uncontested lead, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is a reminder that in a race this size its chance depends entirely on getting a solo breather — has been placed twelve times in thirteen Good-ground starts without a win.
runners_data.comment: Pure Logic ran third last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, while a rating of 96 ranked third of 19 makes her a genuine danger; the chief concern is a trainer without a landing in 24 attempts over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Pirate Island
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse with a poor recent profile (no placed effort in last six starts) and modest Good-ground figures (0 wins, 0 places from 6 comparable runs); distance stretches record and Shane Markey's claim does little to offset lack of current form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Pirate Island nonetheless heads the ratings and brings distance-and-going experience to the table, with a fifth three starts back hinting at better when things click; the 163 lb burden is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Andyourbirdcansing
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a genuine course win on the book (1/20f/GOO) and 14 runs on Good-equivalent ground from 15 starts, making this the ideal surface; needs to settle just off Pure Logic and produce a clean jump at the last to confirm his position as the main prominent threat.
runners_data.comment: Andyourbirdcansing won two starts back but has been unplaced on her most recent outing, and carrying 162 lb is a stiff ask; she has run over today's distance and going, though her rating of 88 leaves her with plenty to find on the figures.

runners_data.name: Maxicourt
runners_data.note: Hold-up five-year-old in reasonable form (placed three of last five on Good), consistent over similar trips; Conor Smithers's 4lb claim helps at OR 89, but the artificially compressed field at Killarney makes it hard to find the daylight his style demands.
runners_data.comment: Maxicourt showed promise with a third three starts back but has been winless in his last five, and at 160 lb he faces a stiff ask; experience over today's trip and going at least counts in his favour.

runners_data.name: Coup d'Essay
runners_data.note: Tagged as a fader in the finish and has shown a tendency to tire, making the 41-day break a concern; only two comparable Good-ground runs from eight attempts, trainer Cromwell in decent 14-day form (6/24) but horse's profile doesn't suit steady-pace races.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts and pulled up most recently, Coup d'Essay faces an uphill task here, though the trainer's 29% strike rate and experience over today's trip offer mild encouragement for this gelding carrying 158 lb.

runners_data.name: Silin Alainn
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map by field congestion, returning from 672 days off — that layoff alone makes a winning run highly speculative regardless of running style; fades in finishes and failed to place in any of five similar-ground starts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for 672 days, Silin Alainn faces a stiff task ranked 14 of 19 on our figures, and a career-high 153 lb adds further concern; going experience is a small plus, and the yard is in decent nick.

runners_data.name: Tedworth
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose best run (a win and a place from 15 Good-ground starts) came when able to settle well off the pace; forced into midfield by the crowded rear, though the 37-day freshener and Michael Kenneally's experience mean he could sneak into contention in a chaotic finish.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win four starts back but has since unseated and finished seventh in his last two, making his current form hard to trust; has run over today's trip and going, and 37 days off at least gives him a fresher look off 153 lb.

runners_data.name: Ballinvasas Best
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent placed form over Good ground (4 times from 6 runs), has been competitive over course-equivalent trips and should slot just behind Pure Logic; Patrick O'Brien takes the ride with no recent trainer activity flagged, which is mildly concerning.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of nineteen, Ballinvasas Best does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, but an unseating last time out and inconsistent recent form make her tough to enthuse over carrying 152 lb.

runners_data.name: Uptaurintop
runners_data.note: Consistent midfield performer (three placed efforts from 13 Good-ground runs) who wears a tongue-tie; naturally a hold-up type corralled closer than ideal by the large field, making his reliable place-form a ceiling rather than a springboard here.
runners_data.comment: Uptaurintop has placed third on three occasions in recent starts but remains yet to win, and while he has run over today's trip and going, carrying 152 lb against higher-ranked rivals makes life difficult for this consistent but elusive sort.

runners_data.name: Laligurash
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a poor recent sequence (U-0780), fades in finishes, and not one Good-ground placing from four attempts — shunted closer to midfield than his true style warrants, and there is little in the form to encourage at this level even if he gets a clearer passage.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Laligurash has yet to win in his last five starts but remains lightly raced with more to offer; carrying 150 lb on his return 29 days later, he merits consideration if bouncing back to form.

runners_data.name: Drumadeise
runners_data.note: Consistent non-finisher (0000U in recent form) with zero placings from five Good-ground runs; natural hold-up type redistributed toward midfield, Dylan Whelan's claim insufficient to compensate for a horse that has shown no ability to get competitive at this standard.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 18 of 19 on our figures, Drumadeise makes for a difficult proposition, her recent sequence featuring an unseating alongside four unplaced efforts; experience on today's going is the one small plus.

runners_data.name: Whatyouwant
runners_data.note: Has a win and a place on Good ground over longer trips (1/25f, 5/25f) suggesting stamina is the weapon; a genuine hold-up runner mapped closer than preferred, but if the pace is honest enough and the field fragments, the 32-day return and proven staying form give him a dark-horse profile in a chaotic finish.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 19 on our figures, Whatyouwant has managed just one win in her last five starts, with a ninth last time out the most recent return, and the weight of 149 lb adds no favours; she does at least arrive fit enough and has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Keyser Smokesy
runners_data.note: Fades in finishes with no wins and no places from six comparable Good-ground runs; a true hold-up type squeezed into midfield, and headgear-free recent form shows no uptick — a difficult proposition at OR 77.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled up and an unseated among them, Keyser Smokesy is hard to fancy from a ranking of 17th of 19 on our figures, though she does return from a 36-day break with going experience in her favour.

runners_data.name: Lake Okeechobee
runners_data.note: Fader in finishes with modest Good-ground figures (0W, 0P from 4 runs) and 74 days off the track; hold-up horse mapped artificially forward, and the combination of a long absence and soft-ground form raising questions about current readiness on Good.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, Lake Okeechobee faces a stiff ask here, with a seventh last time out and a return after 74 days doing little to inspire confidence, though she has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: The Border Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent-style nine-year-old with one win and three places from 15 Good-ground runs, showing course-trip awareness; headgear (hood/cheekpieces) retained, and Danny Power's 4lb claim keeps the weight manageable — likely to sit third or fourth and plug on honestly.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out and winless in his last five starts, The Border Boy is hard to fancy ranked 15 of 19 on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns here on a manageable 143 lb.

runners_data.name: Ballindenisk
runners_data.note: Top weight at OR 95 but no jockey declared and 98 days off track — significant absentee flags; fades in finishes and only 2 comparable Good-ground runs from 5, making this a difficult race to assess even if participation is confirmed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning after a 98-day absence, Ballindenisk faces a stiff ask carrying 166 lb, though he has run over today's going before and that experience offers some small comfort for connections.

runners_data.name: Mr Macphisto
runners_data.note: Prominent-style ten-year-old with two wins and four places from 15 Good-ground runs — the most experienced horse in the field over comparable ground; tongue-tie retained, 50 days off, but a reliable traveller who could outfox younger rivals if the pace is manageable.
runners_data.comment: Mr Macphisto has experience over today's trip and going, and a third three starts back offers some encouragement, but he has pulled up and fallen in his two most recent outings and remains winless in his last five starts, making him a difficult proposition at 151 lb.

runners_data.name: Mc Swagger
runners_data.note: Top-rated horse in the field at OR 100 but recent form is dire (9-U900) with the only black-type hint buried in the hist; fades in finishes, seven runs on Good without a win, and 37 days since last run — a horse well above its current form curve.
runners_data.comment: Mc Swagger has going experience to call on and returns after 37 days looking fresh, but his recent string of unplaced efforts — including two in his last three starts — makes it hard to ignore that he heads here winless in his last five, and the hefty 171 lb burden is the obvious concern.

races.paceDynamic: Pure Logic is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a 19-runner field, should secure a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front at a sustainable tempo over 2m4f on Good ground at Killarney. The prominent types — Andyourbirdcansing, Ballinvasas Best, Mr Macphisto and The Border Boy — will attempt to track closely, creating a compact early group, but Pure Logic is unlikely to be seriously pressured for the lead. The field holds significantly more hold-up and midfield types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Laligurash, Tedworth, Silin Alainn, Uptaurintop, Keyser Smokesy, Lake Okeechobee, Whatyouwant and Drumadeise are all genuine hold-up horses who will be forced into tighter mid-pack positions than they prefer, creating a congested chasing pack. With one uncontested front-runner dictating a steady, honest pace, this shape classically suits prominent racers who can travel fluidly just off the leader without expending energy, and who have the resolution to quicken from the second-last — hold-up horses mapped artificially closer to midfield gain nothing from this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pure Logic Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Logic leads uncontested at a steady tempo and the prominent chasers track without incident to the turn for home.
scenarios.body: Pure Logic sets a controlled fractions on the front end while Andyourbirdcansing and Ballinvasas Best travel comfortably in second and third, with the race developing into a two-flight stamina test from the home turn; horses who jump and travel prominently without burning early reserves have a decisive edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Quicken Past
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Logic fades after the second-last and a prominent chaser looms up with a well-timed move from just off the pace.
scenarios.body: The steady gallop suits a horse that has been lobbing in third or fourth, produces a clean jump at the last and outstays rivals on the run-in; Andyourbirdcansing's course-and-distance win and Mr Macphisto's experience over similar trips make them the main beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace picks up sharply from three out, stringing the field and leaving genuine mid-pack types with ground to make up from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A horse tracking just behind the front group manages to weave through a tiring pack and catch exhausted leaders on the run-in; Deise Crystal and Maxicourt have the form credentials to run on from midfield, though neither is a natural closer and the steadily-run pace works against a dramatic late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Large Field
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant interference, fallers or a scrambled mid-race tempo that fragments the field into disconnected groups.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners over hurdles on a sharp track, a melee in the chasing pack could benefit any horse that avoided trouble and jumps cleanly into the straight; Pure Logic could be swept up in front-group traffic if the pace suddenly collapses, opening the race to opportunists.

watchPoints.text: Pure Logic must be monitored closely at the start — if any prominent runner (Andyourbirdcansing, Ballinvasas Best) breaks sharply and contests the lead, the supposedly uncontested gallop evaporates and the pace dynamic shifts materially.

With 19 runners over hurdles on Killarney's sharp track, watch for crowding and interference at the first two flights as the large chasing pack compresses — horses like Tedworth and Whatyouwant, forced closer than natural, are most vulnerable to losing position through no fault of their own.

Ballindenisk (OR 95, no jockey declared, 98 days off) is a latent danger if a last-minute booking appears — the top weight with a 0W/0P recent profile is likely a non-runner, but confirmation before the off matters for field reading.

Mc Swagger's OR 100 makes it the highest-rated horse in the race on paper, but the 9-U900 form sequence and seven winless Good-ground runs suggest the rating is a historical artefact — watch whether any market support emerges that contradicts the bare form.

Andyourbirdcansing's record of 14 runs on Good-equivalent ground from 15 starts, combined with a course win at this distance, means any drift in its price in the final market move is a meaningful signal worth tracking before post time.

races.name: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Duke Silver
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for J J Slevin and Joseph O'Brien with solid good-ground form (two wins, four places in 15 similar-going runs); the 2m6½f trip suits his staying profile and coming off a 50-day break he should be fresh — the U last time is the only flag to note.
runners_data.comment: Duke Silver shaped with plenty of promise when third two starts back, and has run over today's trip and going, making him a live threat off a mark of 132; the weight of 166 lb and that unseated last time are the key concerns.

runners_data.name: Jazzy Matty
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner, but going rate tagged as racing out of role (STYLE_FIT 0.93) and a 134-day absence is significant; controls this race tactically but her chance of winning depends on whether she retains enough stamina to sustain it over 2m6½f.
runners_data.comment: Jazzy Matty has run over today's trip and going before, and his second two starts back shows he can get competitive, with a rating of 144 making him the one to beat; the 134-day absence is the only question mark for this yet-to-score gelding carrying 164 lb.

runners_data.name: Millstream Lady
runners_data.note: Two hurdle wins on good ground at 2m3f-2m6f make the trip and going ideal, and she has placed repeatedly from hold-up positions; the 237-day layoff for McNamara's runner is the primary concern — watch market support for freshness signals.
runners_data.comment: Millstream Lady showed her class with a win three starts back and a second two starts back, and she has experience of today's distance and going to call on; the concern is a 237-day absence, and whether she returns to peak sharpness first time out.

runners_data.name: Magnor Glory
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old who races prominently and has strong good-ground credentials (15/15 similar-going runs), with a hat-trick of good-ground wins in his record; the OR of 124 and consistent top-five finishes suggest he is a realistic player if he gets a clean prominent slot behind Jazzy Matty.
runners_data.comment: Magnor Glory has distance and going experience in his favour and returns after a 36-day break carrying 158 lb, yet a third four starts back offers the best recent encouragement for a gelding winless in his last five; the pulled-up run three starts back remains the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Plontier
runners_data.note: Fitted with a tongue-strap and running just seven days after his last outing, this ten-year-old hold-up type has a modest record in similar going (0 wins, 1 place from 11 runs) and was a remote seventh last time; the quick turnaround and flat recent form make him a clear outsider.
runners_data.comment: Plontier landed a win four starts back but has offered little since, finishing fourth, sixth, and seventh in his last three outings; at 157 lb he faces a stiff weight task, though he rates fifth of these on our figures and returns on a quick seven-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Londonofficecallin
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap fitted, three good-ground wins including one at 2m in similar conditions; wants a prominent position but may find several rivals ahead of him in the scrimmage — Gavin Cromwell's 6/24 two-week strike rate is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 14 on our figures, Londonofficecallin makes it hard to build a case, with two fifth-place finishes either side of a runner-up effort in his last three starts; he has experience over today's trip and going, a trainer firing at 29%, but the burden of 154 lb looks daunting.

runners_data.name: Rebel Budz
runners_data.note: Won at 2m4f on soft and placed at 2m2f on good — the step up to 2m6½f looks an asset for this prominent racer who has been off for 231 days; limited recent form data (only three historical runs visible) means fitness is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Rebel Budz arrives after a lengthy 231-day absence and is ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, making him hard to fancy in this company despite a second two starts back and a win on his most recent outing.

runners_data.name: Talk In The Park
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with two good-ground placings at 2m1f-2m2f; the step up to 2m6½f is new ground and the recent run 22 days ago is a positive — form figures show a P (pulled-up) lurking in the last five, which tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, Talk In The Park does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 22 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; the 154 lb burden, plus that pulled up and unseated on his card, are the obvious concerns.

runners_data.name: Frankendael
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose natural role sits further back than his mapped midfield position — the field's depth of hold-up types has pushed him forward on the map, though in reality he is likely to race off the back; seven runs on good or similar going yield zero wins and only two places, which is the more important handicap here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Frankendael at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and a third four starts back offers a flicker of encouragement, though consecutive sixth-place finishes more recently and a 151 lb burden make progress hard to foresee.

runners_data.name: My Trump Card
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type who has found only 0 wins and 0 places in three similar-going runs; placed further forward on the map than his genuine style warrants given the volume of hold-up horses in this field — the form figures of 560-06 tell a clear recent story.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of fourteen here, My Trump Card does at least bring going experience and a fitness edge having run just 12 days ago, though 149 lb is a stiff burden for a horse yet to find the winner's enclosure in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Jupiter Du Gite
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with all five recent runs on heavy or soft going — good is an unknown surface for him and the hg flag (hood/tongue) is worth noting; the second last time on soft is his best recent effort and a good-ground switch raises a legitimate question mark.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out after 37 days off the track, Jupiter Du Gite has run over today's trip and carries 147 lb, but he remains winless in his last five starts, with a fourth three starts back the best he has managed beyond that runner-up effort.

runners_data.name: Stormbreaker
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse redistributed forward on the map purely due to field congestion at the rear; three zeros from his last three completed runs and a pulled-up on the last card suggest he is well below the required level regardless of where he settles.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts — a sequence that includes a pull-up — and with the trainer yet to land a winner in 24 attempts over the past fortnight, Stormbreaker faces stiff questions at 147 lb despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Hees Dynamite
runners_data.note: Four wins on good ground from 10 similar-going runs for McNamara's yard, with two recent wins at 2m2f-2m4f; a prominent racer with a genuine stamina profile and a live each-way chance if he can secure the box seat — 24 days since last run is a normal gap.

runners_data.name: Butch Coolidge
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer who is mapped to midfield only because the field is saturated with pace — in reality he is likely to try to push forward and meet traffic; the six-year-old won at 2m2f on good ground and is lightly weighted at OR 102, but the style compromise is real here.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 14 on our figures, Butch Coolidge has been out of the frame in his last three starts and, despite a win four starts back, his recent profile makes him very hard to fancy, even if he does return quickly and has experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Jazzy Matty is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field at 2m6½f on good ground, and with no genuine rival likely to press from the outset, she should be able to control tempo from flag to finish at a pace of her own choosing — sustainable and unhurried over this staying trip. Behind her, Magnor Glory, Londonofficecallin, Hees Dynamite and Jupiter Du Gite all want to race prominently, meaning the positions directly behind the leader will be fiercely contested in the early stages, compressing the midfield. The field holds more prominent-type runners than can all secure their natural position: Magnor Glory and Hees Dynamite are most likely to actually land the prominent slots given their class and recent form, while Butch Coolidge and Frankendael will find themselves shuffled further back than ideal. A controlled, single-paced gallop over 2m6½f on good ground strongly favours genuine staying hold-up horses who can travel off a modest tempo and produce a sustained run from two out — horses like Duke Silver and Millstream Lady who can settle, travel and pick off tiring rivals in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jazzy Matty Controls, Stayers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Jazzy Matty leads unchallenged at a fair but sustainable gallop and the race develops into a searching but rhythmic test from three out.
scenarios.body: Jazzy Matty dictates on her own terms but 2m6½f on good ground is stamina-genuine, and the hold-up horses who settle well will be powering past the early leaders in the final half-mile; Duke Silver's consistent form over 2m-3m on good ground and J J Slevin's tactical awareness make him a prime beneficiary of this shape, as does Millstream Lady who has won at this trip in good-ground conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Dries Up, Front Rank Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Jazzy Matty sets an overly moderate tempo and the race becomes falsely run, allowing prominent horses to coast and kick from the home turn.
scenarios.body: With very little pressure on the leader, horses travelling prominently can conserve energy and sprint from two out, negating the stamina advantage of deeper hold-up horses; Magnor Glory's consistent top-five finishes on good ground and Hees Dynamite's two wins over similar distances make them the likeliest to capitalise from the box seat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Contested Early, Hold-Up Sweeps
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners scrimmage for position in the early stages and the pace lifts enough to string out the field, leaving genuine hold-up types to sweep through late.
scenarios.body: A genuine early battle for prominent spots behind Jazzy Matty would raise the gallop and hollow out the leaders, handing the final two hurdles to horses with a clean passage from the rear; Millstream Lady, absent 237 days but a two-time winner at this type of trip on good ground, and Talk In The Park who placed twice at similar distances, could make a forward move count.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Longshot Lands
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners clash hard for position early, the pace becomes extreme, and attrition through the field opens the door to a lower-rated stayer.
scenarios.body: A scenario requiring significant chaos and errors from the market leaders is inherently low probability, but a well-handicapped six-year-old in Butch Coolidge — though mapped away from his natural position here — could find daylight if a race of genuine quality attrition sets up from the front; Londonofficecallin's three wins on good ground and stamina credentials keep him in the picture at long odds in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Jazzy Matty's 134-day absence combined with a STYLE_FIT flag means she may fade as the sole leader over 2m6½f — watch her jumping fluency from the third-last hurdle as a key tell on whether she can sustain the front.

Millstream Lady's 237-day layoff makes her a significant watch in the paddock and early market moves — if she shows freshness she has the profile to be dangerous, but a ring-rusty run-back is an equally plausible outcome at this price of absence.

The battle for prominent positions directly behind Jazzy Matty between Magnor Glory, Hees Dynamite and Londonofficecallin could create a pocket of early interference — runners drawn wide in the pack, particularly Duke Silver, may need a patient Slevin to navigate cleanly.

Jupiter Du Gite has not run on good ground in his last five starts — all have been on heavy or soft — making his performance here a genuine unknown; if the going remains genuinely good throughout, his chance hinges entirely on how well he handles the surface switch.

Butch Coolidge, Frankendael and My Trump Card are all running out of their natural position due to field congestion — observe early positioning to see whether any of them manage to reclaim their preferred role, as that would significantly alter the tactical picture.

races.name: Moynihan Scaffolding Ltd. And The Warehouse Café Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Bowensonfire
runners_data.note: Strong recent flat-speed profile (OR 120), Gordon Elliott yard in good form (T14: 4/39), but this horse's natural instinct is to race prominently — squeezed into a midfield slot by the race map, meaning its true pace advantage may not be fully exploited here.|
runners_data.comment: Bowensonfire arrives here in good heart after a second last time out, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions to call upon; the concern is that 166 lb is a hefty burden to carry against this field.

runners_data.name: Daddy Long Legs
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained OR 120 with solid Good-ground credentials (sim-going: 10/15, 3W8P), but as a genuine front-runner by inclination, being held up in midfield against his nature is a significant tactical obstacle in this shape — approach with caution.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and lightly raced he may not be, but Daddy Long Legs arrives on the back of a win two starts back and a runner-up last time out, and with his trainer firing at 40% over the past fortnight, he looks the one to beat here carrying 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Eastmore
runners_data.note: Best similar-going record in the field (sim-going: 14/15, 2W8P), consistent recent form (2-3218) with a Killarney win over 16f on Good — naturally prominent and well-placed to exploit the measured pace set by Kilgame without having to race out of role.|
runners_data.comment: Eastmore won two starts back but has finished eighth on his most recent outing, and ranked last of six on our figures he faces a stiff ask under 166 lb, though he does have experience of today's trip and going to call on.

runners_data.name: Kilgame
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will set the tempo throughout, but had a break of 107 days and the STYLE_FIT tag suggests that at OR 120 in this company, dictating may expose rather than protect — jumping will be key given the hg:t headgear.|
runners_data.comment: Kilgame won two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims on conditions, and at 166 lb he arrives fit enough to threaten after 107 days off — though that recent unseating exit is the one question mark his supporters must answer.

runners_data.name: Putapoundinthejar
runners_data.note: Two wins from last three runs (form: 05-311) on Good ground and a genuine hold-up style makes this the most credible deep closer in the field — A J Martin's yard is quiet (T14: 0/5), but the horse's form is the most progressive and it only requires a true pace to find its range.|
runners_data.comment: Putapoundinthejar arrives in fine heart, winning two of his last five starts including back-to-back victories, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions — the chief concern is whether 166 lb at the weights will blunt his momentum.

runners_data.name: Therellbguddaysyet
runners_data.note: Oldest horse in the field at 10, lowest OR at 103, and with a modest recent form string (4-58P5) — a genuine hold-up type but dependent on a strong pace that this race shape is unlikely to deliver, making its chance peripheral at best.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked fifth of six on our figures, Therellbguddaysyet faces a stiff ask at 166 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a reasonable 24-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Kilgame is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over the 2m1f trip on Good ground at Killarney. Bowensonfire and Daddy Long Legs are both natural prominent-racing types but are redistributed to midfield in the map because the race cannot accommodate all of them at the head of affairs — Eastmore, who has the most consistent recent form and the best similar-going record in this field, is the likeliest horse to actually secure a prominent berth alongside or just behind Kilgame. The hold-up pair Putapoundinthejar and Therellbguddaysyet will be further back, meaning the finish hinges on whether the tempo set by Kilgame is soft enough to be caught or stiff enough to stretch the field. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a measured pace — most favours true prominent racers who can travel just off the leader and pounce in the straight, rather than deep hold-up horses needing a stronger gallop to bring them into play.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kilgame Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Kilgame sets a controlled pace and a horse travelling just behind can challenge from the second-last fence.
scenarios.body: Kilgame controls from flag to flag, and the winner emerges from the chasing pack travelling prominently — the measured tempo means energy is conserved for a late surge in the straight, favouring horses who tracked the pace rather than came from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Kilgame sets a genuinely slow pace and is never seriously pressured, conserving enough to outstay all rivals.
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace challenger, Kilgame could exploit the lack of pressure by lobbing along in front and jumping fluently throughout, making the race too easy for those behind to organise a serious challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the front rank tires in the final half-mile, allowing the hold-up horses to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: Putapoundinthejar's recent winning form and winning record over this type of trip on Good ground makes it the most dangerous of the hold-up types, and a genuinely run race would bring it into contention from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Tactical Race
scenarios.trigger: If early positioning causes interference or horses race in unfamiliar roles, scrambling the expected shape.
scenarios.body: Bowensonfire and Daddy Long Legs, both natural prominent-goers compressed into midfield, could unsettle the race rhythm if they push forward and crowd Kilgame — the ensuing tactical confusion could produce an unpredictable result with stamina-tested form figures misleading.

watchPoints.text: Eastmore — if it secures a prominent position behind Kilgame as expected, its superior similar-going record (14/15) makes it the principal danger to all runners in Scenario A.

Putapoundinthejar — two recent wins and a genuine hold-up style give it a live chance if the tempo quickens, but it must be noted Daniel King's trainer is near-silent (T14: 0/5), which could dampen confidence in its preparation.

Kilgame — 107 days off the track is a significant concern for a front-runner in a beginners' chase; a jumping error or fitness lapse could collapse the expected race shape entirely and open the door for hold-up horses.

Bowensonfire and Daddy Long Legs — both are natural prominent-going horses mapped to midfield; if either pushes forward early and challenges Kilgame for the lead, the tempo rises sharply and Scenario C closers become far more dangerous.

Therellbguddaysyet — with OR 103 and a pull of 17lbs in notional terms at the same weight, connections may adopt a forcing tactic rather than their usual hold-up approach, which would be worth monitoring in the parade ring and early strides.

races.name: Old Market Lane Traders Novice Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Uncle Pat
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained eight-year-old with solid Good-ground form (two wins, five places from 15 similar-going runs) who wants to travel prominently just off the pace; the 43-day break is not a concern for this yard and his OR of 139 makes him the class anchor in this field.

runners_data.name: Butch Cassidy
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's six-year-old is the race's sole front-runner and will face zero pressure setting the tempo — his recent Good-ground win confirms suitability, though 105 days off the track is the one question mark over his readiness to sustain the gallop over 2m7½f.

runners_data.name: Yoradreamer
runners_data.note: Ran 22 days ago and arrives the freshest in terms of recent racecourse fitness; a Mullins-trained prominent type on going he handles, though his record of 0 wins from 9 Good-ground attempts (2 places) suggests he tends to find one too good rather than win outright.

runners_data.name: Battle Of Benburb
runners_data.note: Form reads P7PP-0 and OR of 77 marks him as the class inferior; naturally a prominent racer, he is pushed into midfield by the competition for those positions — his STYLE_FIT of 0.93 signals he will be racing out of role, which combined with his modest form makes him a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Emily Love
runners_data.note: Kennedy takes the mount for Elliott on this seven-year-old who carries a genuinely strong winning record on Good ground (4W from 11 similar-going runs); a natural prominent racer shown at hold-up due to field redistribution, so she will need Kennedy to place her closer than the map suggests to give her every chance.

races.paceDynamic: Butch Cassidy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse novice chase over 2m7½f and will set a controlled, solo tempo on Good ground at Killarney — with no rival capable of seriously contesting the lead, he faces zero pressure and can dictate his own rhythm throughout. Uncle Pat and Yoradreamer are both prominent types who will sit close to the pace just off Butch Cassidy's shoulder, creating a compact early order. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position: Battle Of Benburb is a genuine prominent runner redistributed to midfield, and Emily Love is a prominent horse mapped to hold-up, meaning neither is likely to race where they are most effective. A sustainable, galloping tempo over this long trip on Good turf strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in behind a relaxed leader and attack from a controlled position — prominent-to-lead profiles are the primary beneficiaries of this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Butch Cassidy Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Butch Cassidy bowls along uncontested and sets an even, unhurried gallop throughout the 2m7½f trip.
scenarios.body: Butch Cassidy dictates from the front on his own terms, conserves energy through the back straight, and kicks at his leisure jumping the final fences — his recent Goodwood form win on Good ground underlines the suitability of these conditions. Horses who travel prominently such as Uncle Pat and Yoradreamer can stalk but may lack the finish to reel in a leader who has never been asked a question.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Butch Cassidy's long layoff (105 days) blunts his sharpness and Uncle Pat or Yoradreamer track him closely enough to pounce at the final fence.
scenarios.body: Uncle Pat, with his excellent Good-ground record and Mullins/King combination, is ideally positioned to swoop from just off the pace if the leader weakens on the run-in after jumping 18 fences. Yoradreamer's recent run (22 days ago) gives him a fitness edge that could tell in the closing stages of this stamina test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Emily Love Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and Emily Love, a natural prominent type racing from further back, makes up ground over the final fences.
scenarios.body: Emily Love's strong form record (4 wins, 9 places on Good ground) and Jack Kennedy's ability to produce late runs give her a chance if the front-runners tire dramatically over the extended trip. However, as a redistributed prominent type racing further back than suits her, she must overcome a positional disadvantage — discount this scenario accordingly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Shakeup
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or departures among the lead group scramble the race order and produce an open contest in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Battle Of Benburb, although running out of his natural role from midfield, could theoretically benefit from chaos reducing the field — his course form on Good ground is at least noted. This scenario requires multiple things to go wrong for the principals and is highly unlikely given the small, experienced field.

watchPoints.text: Watch Butch Cassidy's jumping closely in the early stages — if he makes errors at the novice fences and loses his lead position, the entire race dynamic collapses and the other prominent types will flood the front.

Uncle Pat's last run was a distant seventh; if he shows any sign of not travelling fluently behind Butch Cassidy in the first mile, his chance of hitting the frame from a prominent position evaporates.

Emily Love must be tracked in the betting market — if Jack Kennedy elects to push her forward from the outset rather than accept a hold-up role, she could effectively compress the lead group and turn this into a more contested race than anticipated.

Battle Of Benburb raced with headgear (p) and has failed to complete or finish close in recent outings — monitor him at the first few fences as he represents a fall or unseating risk in a field of only five runners.

With the entire field rated Good-going OK and Killarney's going report confirming genuine Good across all races today, no runner faces a going-related disadvantage — the race is likely to be decided on class, jumping, and positioning rather than ground suitability.

races.name: Canella Lane Handicap Steeplechase (Listed)

runners_data.name: Senecia
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Vincent Halley and Phillip Enright; 1 win and 3 places from 15 similar-ground runs suggests solid course-type form, with recent pull-up and fall in form string a concern, but the 2m5f trip and Good ground are squarely in range at OR 152.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win two starts back before unseating last time, and Senecia has experience of today's trip and going to call on; at 166 lb he faces a stiff weight task, but his rating marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Solitary Man
runners_data.note: E Bolger's front-runner arrives in form with 2 wins in last 5, has a strong going record (3W6P on similar ground), and gets to dictate here unchallenged — but the STYLE_FIT flag suggests he is in reality operating at the limit of his comfort zone in a more competitive field than he usually controls.
runners_data.comment: Solitary Man has winning form in his recent starts, scoring two starts back, and he returns on fit terms after 24 days off with experience of today's trip and conditions on his side; the main concern is the 152 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Jalila Moriviere
runners_data.note: Top-weight for Mullins and Mark Walsh, a powerful booking; her recent form includes two placed efforts at 2m and 2m4f on Good, and she handles this surface well (1W3P in 6 similar-ground runs), though her tongue tie and a slightly step up in class at Listed level are worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive runner-up finishes two and three starts back underline her strong claims here, and a trainer firing at 40% over the past fortnight adds significant confidence; the risk is that she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Boston Rover
runners_data.note: Has won three of his last five on Good or similar, including a run over 2m4f on Good going; Gordon Elliott's runner is proven at this trip range, and the 43-day absence is the only note of caution — Josh Williamson takes a 3lb claim to offset the layoff concern.
runners_data.comment: Boston Rover won three of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories three and four runs ago, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions, but a fifth last time and 43 days off since raise fitness questions under a hefty 147 lb.

runners_data.name: She's A Fine Wine
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's mare is a prolific winner on Good ground (4W6P in 12 similar-going runs) and her recent wins at shorter trips suggest she possesses the tactical pace to burn if used aggressively; the tongue tie is a familiar fitment and Darragh O'Keeffe is a positive booking.
runners_data.comment: She's A Fine Wine has back-to-back wins in her recent form, but that eighth last time out is a concern, she ranks ninth of twelve on our figures, and 144 lb is a stiff burden against this field.

runners_data.name: Ballybawn Belter
runners_data.note: Simon Torrens partners this hold-up type for Liz Doyle, who has no wins from 9 similar-going efforts — the form string includes a pull-up last time and the mare appears notably better on Soft; Good ground looks like a genuine going concern.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out is the obvious concern, but third two starts back shows she retains ability when completing; her win came five starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and going, with 141 lb the key query on her current mark of 127.

runners_data.name: Mousey Brown
runners_data.note: McLoughlin's nine-year-old races in a tongue pad and has struggled to convert his placed form into wins — zero wins in 11 similar-ground runs despite two placed efforts; Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim helps but this is a hold-up horse who needs the pace to collapse for him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts yet clearly capable of mixing it with the principals, Mousey Brown showed she belongs at this level with a second two starts back, and she has experience of today's trip and going; the weight of 140 lb is the obvious question mark.

runners_data.name: Rexem
runners_data.note: Ran only 14 days ago and has strong recent form (1-2-3 in last 4 on Good), giving him fitness and going profile advantages; Joshua Halford's 7lb claim is meaningful, and 12 similar-ground runs with 2 wins and 5 places make Rexem quietly consistent at this level despite a lower OR of 124.
runners_data.comment: Rexem won last time out and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround, but he rates the outsider of the field on our figures, ranked tenth of twelve, and that gulf makes him hard to fancy despite his recent victory and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Drumgill
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan's seven-year-old is a natural hold-up performer whose true style has been pushed forward on the map by redistribution — in reality he is likely to race from the rear as usual; zero wins on similar going in 8 comparable runs, and a STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations if he cannot get back to his natural late position.
runners_data.comment: Drumgill showed some promise when third last time out and returns here on a quick 14-day turnaround with distance and going experience in his favour, yet he remains winless in his last six starts and his ranking of eighth of twelve suggests he faces a stiff task at 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Lisleigh Lad
runners_data.note: Ms Broderick's prominent racer has good similar-going form (3W6P in 12 runs) and placed in his last visit to this trip range; the form string shows a win at 2m followed by a fall and a pull-up, so soundness and jumping reliability are the watchpoints before the field has even reached the second last.
runners_data.comment: Ranked toward the foot of the assessments on these figures, Lisleigh Lad is hard to fancy off an unplaced effort last time, though he has experience of today's distance and going and a win two starts back keeps connections hopeful.

runners_data.name: Hermino AA
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent in style but mapped to midfield here because the field is saturated with forward-going types — a blinkers wearer who is unlikely to secure his natural position; OR 122 and zero wins in 7 similar-ground runs in recent history make this a difficult proposition even if the pace shapes up correctly.
runners_data.comment: Hermino AA arrives on the back of a win two starts ago, has experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 131 marks him out as a leading player, though that unplaced effort last time is the concern.

runners_data.name: West Away
runners_data.note: Collins's hold-up horse arrives fresh on 14 days, has 2 wins on Good ground in 11 similar runs, and showed a fine 3rd at 2m3f recently; though a natural rear-of-field operator, the redistribution note means he may be forced forward — if he does get back to his true position, his fitness and going profile make him quietly interesting.
runners_data.comment: West Away has shown flickers of ability — a winner last time out and a third two starts back — but his overall profile in recent starts is patchy, and ranked last on our figures at 140 lb, he faces a stiff ask here.

races.paceDynamic: Solitary Man is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no significant rival pressing for the lead, is set to control this race at a measured, sustainable gallop from the front over 2m5f on Good ground at Killarney. Boston Rover, Jalila Moriviere, She's A Fine Wine, and Lisleigh Lad are all prominent-style runners who will track closely, creating a compact and moderately contested early tempo rather than a true test of stamina. This field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Hermino AA, Drumgill, and West Away are genuine prominent or hold-up horses who are unlikely to secure their preferred positions and will be forced to race in unfamiliar territory. With a lone front-runner dictating a controlled pace, this race shape strongly favours the prominent racers stalking just off Solitary Man, who will be in the ideal position to pounce from the second fence out without having burned energy fighting for position early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Solitary Man sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the horses tracking closely off the pace have the most to gain from the controlled tempo.
scenarios.body: Jalila Moriviere, Boston Rover, and She's A Fine Wine all possess the tactical cruising speed to sit a length or two off Solitary Man before taking it up from two out, and a true-run Good-ground pace over this trip plays right into their hands.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and Solitary Man jumps beautifully throughout, building enough of a cushion that no one can close the gap from the home turn.
scenarios.body: With 12 runners and a bunch of prominent types bottled up behind him, Solitary Man could exploit any positional confusion among his rivals if he pings his fences and extends the advantage approaching the final two obstacles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong early — perhaps through Boston Rover or She's A Fine Wine pressing Solitary Man — and the prominent brigade burns each other out.
scenarios.body: Senecia and Mousey Brown, who are genuine hold-up types, would benefit from a contested gallop that brings the field back to them at the top of the straight, though both lack recent winning form on this ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Redistribution
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded prominent group causes interference, jumping errors, or positional scrambling that disrupts the expected race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Horses forced out of their natural role — Drumgill, Hermino AA, and West Away — face the steepest uphill task here, but a messy race could see one of the more unexposed angles like Rexem, who has winning form on this ground, emerge from the disorder.

watchPoints.text: Solitary Man sets every fraction of this race — if he pings his fences and extends the lead turning for home, the prominent brigade must commit early or risk running out of race; watch whether Boston Rover or She's A Fine Wine is sent up to pressurise him, as that decision will determine whether the front-runner holds on or is swallowed up.

Jalila Moriviere and Boston Rover are the two highest-profile prominent types immediately behind Solitary Man — both are trained by powerful yards with in-form jockeys, and a duel between them for the best tracking position could stretch the field and hurt both if they get into a battle from the outset.

Lisleigh Lad's form string shows a win followed by a fall (F) then a pull-up (0) — jumping confidence is a live concern in a Listed steeplechase at this trip, and any jumping mistake from him could cause interference to the prominent group stacked closely behind Solitary Man.

Drumgill, Hermino AA, and West Away are all mapped out of their natural positions due to redistribution — if any of them barge forward to try to reclaim their preferred spot, it creates a scramble among the 12 runners in the early stages that could unbalance the race shape entirely.

Good ground is consistent across the full Killarney card and is unlikely to change; Ballybawn Belter's record on Good is markedly weaker than on Soft (0W3P vs 1W elsewhere), making her an in-running drifter to monitor if the market shortens her on the basis of her yard's overall strike rate.

runners_data.name: Farney Bridge
runners_data.comment: Farney Bridge won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a clear threat at the head of the ratings; the main risk is that weight of 168 lb on a 37-day break could blunt the edge of his winning momentum.

runners_data.name: Rokanako
runners_data.comment: Rokanako is lightly raced and open to plenty of improvement, with a win two starts back the brightest note in his limited form; freshened up after 49 days away, he carries 168 lb on his return.

runners_data.name: Teofil
runners_data.comment: Teofil arrives in excellent nick, winning last time out and finishing second two starts back, and he has run over today's trip before; a 26-day freshener looks ideal and he is our pick despite not heading the ratings.

runners_data.name: Loughtown
runners_data.comment: Loughtown has pulled up on one occasion and been unplaced in his other two recent starts, leaving him yet to score, though his lightly raced profile keeps him open to improvement; carrying 161 lb on return from a 50-day break, connections will hope that profile counts for something here.

runners_data.name: Mystic Bridge
runners_data.comment: Mystic Bridge makes his debut carrying 161 lb, lightly raced and entirely unexposed, leaving him open to considerable improvement; yet to score, everything remains unknown about his ceiling and he warrants close watching on first appearance.

runners_data.name: Old Court
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Old Court resumes after 259 days off the track following a pulled-up effort last time, and with just the one recent start on record he remains lightly raced and yet to score, though there is clearly more to discover.

runners_data.name: Emergency Man
runners_data.comment: Emergency Man shaped with plenty of promise when runner-up last time out, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions to call on; the concern is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Ringroan
runners_data.comment: Ringroan makes his debut carrying 158 lb, and as an unraced gelding he is entirely unexposed with every question still to be answered — open to any amount of improvement on this first start.

runners_data.name: Lady Boudica
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Lady Boudica returns after 170 days off yet to score, and her sole recent start ended in a pull-up; connections will be hoping a fresher campaign unlocks better from this lightly raced filly carrying 151 lb.
